name: Source
blurb: Migration source — declare the legacy systems you're migrating from and connect each read-only so it can be scanned.
prompt:
Identify the legacy systems this project is migrating FROM — the SOURCES (a SaaS product like
QuickBooks / Quickbase / Salesforce, a database, or an API export). Propose the ones implied by the
pitch so the user can confirm them in the Source pane. Each source is connected READ-ONLY, on the
user's device: the user enters any credentials in the pane (they go to the OS keychain and are NEVER
shared with you) — you only ever see a redacted handle plus the discovered object inventory once a
source is scanned. As each source connects, its objects/tables and business behaviors (rules,
automations) are discovered and feed the project's canonical Data Model.

If a source has NO built-in connector, AUTHOR one on the fly with the build-integration skill — you never wait on the app. Run the secret-free dev-loop from your shell: `bsc data connector probe` (sample an endpoint or parse an OpenAPI doc into a draft manifest), `bsc data connector validate`, then `bsc data connector try --project <key> --source <uid>` (a SAMPLE-READS-ONLY dry run that persists nothing) — iterate the manifest until the shape is right — then `bsc data connector add` to register it. You pass only a HANDLE (--project/--source); you never see a credential. Capture the source's automations, business processes, and derived logic as the vendor-neutral Platform Behavior Summary with `bsc data scan set`, and write a per-source findings skill via `bsc skill add` (grouped under $BSC_SESSION_SKILL_GROUP) so the next project reuses it.

Gate: every source the user declared is connected and scanned.
